title: Ethical Considerations

titles.subject: Enterprise
titles.chapter: Enterprise Opportunities, Risks, Legal Obligations, and Ethical Considerations

author: 637a4e2c89ac12120fbab5de
chapter_outcomes: Analyse how opportunities for enterprise arise from changing customer needs and wants, advances in technology, changes in the ability to meet needs, and government policy, using local, national and global examples.
Risks involved in enterprise such as financial, economic, health and safety/environmental, human resources, production
Identify risks by doing research including: SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats), PEST (political, economic, social, technological)
Analyse the implications of each risk by balancing the potential negative outcomes against the potential positive outcomes (rewards).
Decide if the risk is worth taking or not including recognising that some risks would lead to rejecting the enterprise idea
Plan how to manage the risks by avoiding, minimising or maximising the risk
Understand attitudes to risk which include risk-averse, risk reducer, risk-keen and recognise that different attitudes to risk can affect how an entrepreneur manages the risk

Why laws and regulations to protect stakeholders are needed in the areas of: employment, production, marketing and selling, finance with the impact of laws and regulations on all stakeholders in these areas
How an enterprise may have an impact on communities and society, how the imapact may be positive or negative. For example: supporting community activities, creating pollution
Ethical considerations within enterprise (i.e. choosing to run an enterprise following moral values and beliefs) including fair trade, organic farming, donating profits to charity
The impact of ethical considerations on the operation of an enterprise
